item.title: Greenlight for SCP - XXXX "The Mood Ring"
item.content:encoded:
Rough first concept for an SPC, tried to keep it simple for my first one by focusing on an artefact that can be classified as safe.

scp concept – The Mood Ring

Class: SAFE

Concept – A simple small men’s ring made of gold. It exacerbates the prime internal flaw of the wearer and broadcasts it to other people nearby. The longer the ring is worn, the worse the effect is. The distance of this broadcast slowly weakens until eventually dissipating after approximately 1KM. When taken off it takes merely seconds for its effect to stop altogether. The bearer does not need to be alive for the ring to work, only be alive when they put the ring on.

For example – if worn by a person who is inherently lazy, then it will slowly make the bearer lazier and more lethargic, eventually causing them to give up altogether and simply sit down and die and broadcast this failure to other people. Someone who is right next to the person in the opening hour would also begin to feel the same before also simply laying down to die, whilst someone who is a mile away would simply feel slightly more tired, or opt for a day on the couch as opposed to the run they were planning. Regardless of the “effect” it was broadcasting, it would have a stronger effect on the person the closer they got to the ring. If the ring was removed the bearer and all the people in the vicinities psychological profile would return to normal, however their physical status would remain unchanged.

Containment – Kept in a standard Artefact lockbox. – needs expanding on…

History of the ring
Discovered by the foundation when asked to assist with the disappearances of experienced jungle explorers and tourists by the Guatemalan government due to the theory that an anomalous source was the cause. Any search team who was sent after them never returned or made a transmission of what they found. The foundation was called in due to the expertise on the anomaly. Investigations led them to a long-lost city belonging to the ancient Aztecs. On arrival they found all the missing hikers as well as many corpses dating back as far as the original conquistadors through to the current missing hikers. An unmanned drone sweep was done of the facility to ensure its safety and samples were taken. Once these samples came back with no airborne or ground contaminants manned teams were sent in to catalogue the bodies and the vast amounts of treasure contained there. The oldest corpses were those of the civilization’s original citizens. Field forensics showed that these people had died from lack of nutrition and possibly water due to bone density loss. The next oldest were the original Spanish explorers to venture this far in, they all showed sign of extreme violence, forensics showing they were involved in a bloodthirsty battle most likely with each other. The leader of the conquistadors was found beneath the still fresh bodies of two hikers who appeared to have killed each other with whatever weapons they could reach. The leader’s right hand was broken, and A small golden ring was discovered next to the body. Not realising what the ring was, it was added to the mountainous pile of gold that was to be sent to another SCP Site for cataloguing and analysis. Whilst here the ring was stolen by a member of staff with the intent to sell it. However, the ring ignited his dominant personality of a man with temper issues. Contact was eventually lost with the facility as the members of facility began to turn on each other over little issues that broke out into viscous fighting. By the time it was resolved almost all the facilities staff were either dead or dying. Further investigating into the facilities logs eventually identified the seemingly unimportant ring to be the cause of everything. Given everything already discovered at the lost-city and the evidence from the destroyed facility they have now determined the ring to be the cause of it.

item.title: SCP-? - "The Sword in the Stone"
item.content:encoded:
Item #: SCP-??

CODENAME: “The Sword in the Stone”

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: The object SCP-?? Is to be kept a medium security facility, and maintained at all moments under a blast proof glass cover of no less than 20mm thickness. Both the sword and the stone are not to be touched except by test subjects. Personnel must obtain authorization from acting site director before interacting with the object, and any attempts to remove the sword from the stone are to be conducted under surveillance of an officer of no lesser than level 2 security clearance.

SCP - ? are only to be removed from storage for testing.

[Sword in the Stone on its containment site]

Description: SCP - ? consists of a simple 12th century medieval sword, inserted into a 1m x 1,5m calcarean stone through a slot carved directed into to the stone’s surface.
The sword itself appears to be made of common steel, oxidized, but analysis in the atomic structure revealed the material does not match any man known metal. All organic parts from the handle appear to be long lost, but the metal in the object seems immune to natural degradation. The sword has no visible marks or decorations, except the old welsh word “Caledfwlch” written in its crossguard. Approximately the first 10cm of the sword’s blade are visible, as the rest of the weapon penetrate the stone.

The stone in composed mostly of common calcium carbonate, with no visible or detectable anomalies, and weighting approximately 300 kilograms. A 4.5cm slot has been carved with chirurgical precision into the stone surface, allowing the sword’s blade to be fitted into the stone with no gaps.

With Latin characters, it is written in old English: "Whoso pulleth out this sword of this stone, is rightwise king born."

Any subject within a radius of 5 meters from SCP - ? will experience moderate anxiety and excitation, and an urge to trying to remove the sword from the stone. Any attempts so far to remove the sword by pulling it from the stone have been unsuccessful. However, it has been noted this urge to remove the sword from the stone dissipates after at least one attempt to pull it out. Subjects who interacted with SCP - ? report an strange feeling of guilt, sadness and nostalgia after their interactions with the object. After the first attempt of removing the sword, the intensity of this “urge” effects will vanish gradually, until the subject became immune to such impulse.
The intensity of this effects appear to be influenced by the subject personal moral inclination, as class D subjects with violent criminal records tend to not be influenced by SCP - ? in the same way, feeling even “aversion” to the idea of touching the sword.

Addendum-1: History
SCP - ? was discovered in the ruins of an old medieval abbey in the British island of Glastonbury. The object was partially buried under the old church's ceiling debris, and was discovered in 2012, by a group of approximately 25 tourists, when a 9-year-old girl accidentally stepped into the sword hilt. The group thought it was some kind of prank, or part of a movie set, and proceed to try to remove the sword from the stone, with no success. A field agent, which was coincidentally spending his vacation in the region, quickly perceived the commotion and started basic containment procedures. The object is kept in a Level 2 secret base in Europe, and a cover story was planted to hide the 2012 incident, as for the public, it was all part of a medieval movie set.

Addendum-2: Disassemble experiment
Test 1: A mechanical arm with a pull force of 10 ton was attached to the sword hilt, to forcibly remove it from the stone. The force applied was amplified gradually until the mechanical implement reached it’s 10 ton limit.

Result: Even at maximum pull strength, SCP - ?-2 continues static, and the sword didn’t move at all, neither the stone, despite the force applied being far greater than the object’s weight.
Test 2: A selection of personal and civilian were allowed to try pulling the sword out. Civilians were administered amnestics after the experiment.

Result: None of the subjects have being successful pulling the sword.
Test 3: A variety of explosives were used against the stone in attempt to destroy it.

Result: SCP - ? remained inert to the explosives, even with the explosions being so strong the actual test room shielding was damaged.
Test 4: Super potent lasers and an industrial high pression water cutter were used in attempt to cut the stone or the sword.

Result: SCP - ? remained inert to water cutter, despite the apparatus being capable of cutting with ease stones of the same material as the SCP. The lasers should not be used again, as refraction effect was observed when the energy bean was directed to the sword, damaging the equipment and the room’s shielding. Further investigation on the metal’s energy reflection properties are to be conducted.

+ More elaborate explanation

What is anomalous about that?

The room itself had its potential danger the deeper it goes, an entity from the colonial era that may or may not be hostile towards any individual that is in the area. The room also may contain cognitive-based hazard that will cause hallucination or even audio disturbances, it tries to repel any foreign individual that is not part of the room with it. I planned to make it seemed like that "Backrooms" kind of vibe towards the rooms that are about to be explored.

where is the narrative.

Now, what is the truth?

This building is a place where Tourists could see the great colonialism, how they managed to steer and changed the way this country look. The deeper as it goes, the more we know about that this colonialism is not humane, full of discriminatory and were built based on misery of the thousand people without being known by the public. The Underground represents the dark side of the events while the upper grounds represents on the sweet fruity results of the colonialism.

A lot of people died, being tortured, slaved, being forced to work for a whole full day without being paid, etc. Just for the sake of "The Great Colonialism Movement" made by the dutch colonies back then. This makes, let's just say, Ghosts from the past still lingering around inside the underground base, because they were shutted down deep down to not let anyone knew what exactly just happened at that time.

This motivates that The Foundation should keep an eye and prevent entities to go through the uppergrounds section, especially the hostile ones, to prevent damages that were caused by those entities towards the public. Because some of the times an entity, lets just say XXXX-1, may come up to the upper grounds that some of the night guards are bothered by their existence and some of them also causes some damage towards the property or even the guards itself.

I'll try to answer this questions regarding the vague-ness or more elaboration on what i meant about this/that towards my explanation.

item.title: Re: Murphy’s Law And The Lucky Ducky.
item.content:encoded:
Would love to give feedback, but there's nothing here to give feedback on. Sure, you have a teen, a duck, and their mutually exclusive viruses, but we have no idea why the teen or the duck are important to the story, and no idea what the viruses do.

That said: Your Central Narrative should go on the page type; this is usually the space where you go into the details of how your SCP works and its story. "Interesting Layout" is not a hook unless you have a truly interesting layout; this is why we should care about the SCP and/or how it fits into the universe as a whole.

I'd love to give you some feedback, but there is just nothing to give feedback on.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea SEEKING GREENLIGHT
item.content:encoded:
1) It's a bad sign when you're actually asking for suggestions on how to fill more space…Also, you don't need to mention how many green lights you need.

2) The hook is actually fine; it's fine to have a whimsical SCP in there every so often, but you may want to build that up a little more. Also, you can truncate most of the elevator pitch; just "How can a hot-air balloon do this?" is fine, although adding a little more as to its purpose would help.

3) The Central Narrative is your biggest problem. Not only do you have some grammatical issues that need to be worked on, but you're also lacking any kind of history with this guy. You need some sort of story, as well as who he would be on the defensive against. You have a hot-air balloon doing a lot of weirdness; there has to be some sort of origin story there. Figure out what it is.

item.title: SCP: The Crusader Pond
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A pond that become active in the winter by becoming frozen. When the pond becomes frozen, ice statues that take the appearance of Templar Knights will form and as a result, people who enter the SCP will be sent into a syndrome like state where they are commit acts of violence towards certain places.

Central Narrative: This takes place in December of 1993 in the woods of Alaska. The SCP Foundation was alerted to a location after strange reports of people worshipping the statues or disappearances relating to them started to become noticed.

As a result, the SCP Foundation attempts to investigate the anomaly and apprehend the cultists by sending four Foundation soldiers but as a result, the soldiers that were sent to the location return back to the Foundation Site attacking the scientists within the site in order to release the other SCPs within it. Of course, this fails and the incident results in the Foundation to be on high alert of the pond and result in them using a Mobile Task Force unit in order to investigate and contain the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The anomaly causes the person who encountered the pond and the statues to be stuck in a trance where they believe that have to do a certain trial or mission to fight for the religious cause. This would be attacking organizations, individuals, locations, etc., that would be considered against their faith.

Additional Notes: I don’t know too much on the MTF but from reading the requirements on the Mobile Task Force article, any user can use an existing MTF for their story if I remember correctly. Of course, you can correct me if I am wrong.

item.title: Re: SCP- Assimilator
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

A humanoid, resembling a male human, consisting of cells with anomalous biological characteristics

I'm…concerned by this list. It makes this SCP idea feel like, super x-man-y: especially considering it's basically just, wolverine without adamantine claws/skeleton.

This feeling becomes stronger when I read your 'Central Narrative' and, instead of an explanation of what the actual SCP article is about or the story you're trying to tell about this dude, I just get more information about what the SCP does and how it hunts and what it wants. The final nail is driven into this coffin when the Hook/Attention grabbed section introduces even more anomalous properties and weird things this does.

At it's core: my issue with this pitch is that you're proposing something that sounds a lot more like your cool fighting OC or a DnD Monster than it does like you're proposing an interesting short story about a weird thing that the Foundation interacts with.

Like, my central question here is: once you've described this thing in the Description of your SCP article, what else are you doing with this? How are you intending to get a reader invested in this monster? How are you intending showing off how cool it is and how the various anomalous things it can do make life difficult for the Foundation? How do you want to make a reader feel?

My hot advice here: put this on the back burner for now. Go away, read a tonne of new SCPs, read a bunch of the guides on writing a narrative in SCPs (see e.g. An exercise in narrative based SCPs or The Journey of Your First SCP: Part II - Narratives & Originality.

Forum thread: SCP- Assimilator

item.title: Re: Semi-Veil breaking Parawatch SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Perhaps a minor concern but this feels…like it goes a bit against the Parawatch writing guide by like, explicitly giving them an anomaly and letting them fully understand what it does. In general, the parawatch vibe is more 'paranoid conspiracy theorists who have no idea what's really going on', and this feels…like it doesn't quite capture that?

I'm also kinda uncertain about this specifically as a SCP article: it feels…kinda like a lot of the fun would be easier to convey if this was a parawatch format where you could open with the post describing how to replicate the anomaly and then have the breathless excitement of them replicating it and having confirmation into like, the paranoia as folk deny it and like the foundation start to shut it down and stuff? Like, obviously you can convey this in a SCP article by including parawatch forum posts but at some point, it'll feel…excessive and like it's unnecessary to include this many; and my concern is that it's very possible it'll feel that way as soon as you include any parawatch posts.

I can't quite put my finger on why but it also just kinda feels like the narrative progression here feels…very generic? Like, it's not exactly the same as a generic containment breach story but it feels like it shares enough in common that it feels like one; the angle of the Foundation shutting down Parawatch feels interesting but it feels like this is framed in a way where we can't really see the weight of that decision because we're seeing stuff from the Foundation's POV.

I guess really it does just come down to me looking at this and thinking it'd feel much better if it was written in the same kinda style as This Is How We Build Revelation, where you blend the prose tale material from the PoV of someone on Parawatch with the forum posts they make, and the responses they get; since all the interesting stuff is happening on the Parawatch side of the story, not the Foundation side.

Also a few minor things:

A simple anomaly is discovered by WWS.

Why WWS? It's such a brief mention that it feels like this is just being done to explain why the Foundation aren't more on the ball here; except the tight relationship between WWS and the Foundation means it still kinda feels weird how little the Foundation know going in; and it also feels…weirdly irrelevant.

The main story of the article comes when a member of the Parawatch community gets their hands on one of the photos and discovers it's anomalous properties.

How do they get their hands on one of the photos?

The article closes out with a note regarding the difficulty of maintaining the veil in the internet age and about being thankful the image wasn't memetic.

This feels too much like it just kinda summarises things we've already seen in the article? Like, you're showing us the difficulty of maintaining the veil; so telling us afterwards feels…unnecessary?

item.title: Re: An Exelent Dentist
item.content:encoded:
Beginning statement

This is hard to understand, like extremely hard to understand. Everything I say may be wrong in your eyes, but, this is only to give you a basic review.

Click me for the review
Click to hide the review

First of all, let me dissect your SCP
The SCP you described is very hard to understand. Your elevator pitch, (Which is supposed to tell me what the SCP is and what makes it anomalous) only touches on the SCP being a family man, and well respected, likely a dentist. The elevator pitch also describes how the SCP is found. Here's the problem, this is an SCP article not an SCP Story, and because you already have given me no clear description of the SCP, it's a big red flag.
The Detective and the Story
Alright so already a problem with the logic of the detective is him getting PTSD from the cases he has been on, and you think he can have those bad thoughts removed by amnestics? There would be no way to dull the PTSD without a psychiatrist, (Thank god you at least did that). The story of this is nothing to special, not good, yet not bad, more or less cliche at worst.


Conclusion
You will need to add a lot to this, mostly fixing up the description of the SCP. I know it's not in the review but the Dentist seems to have no anomalous properties, so why the hell is it an SCP?

item.title: Re: A ball, A god, and A biological something
item.content:encoded:
You're really going to have to expand on this concept a lot more before I can offer really any useful feedback here.

Like, how are the trio related? Why are they being treated as a single SCP object instead of three unrelated ones? How does it tie into 'two ideas they can't get out of their head' and the what's the actual story you're telling here? What is the 'social interaction between the anomalies'? What events do they react to? How does this all come together to tell a compelling, cohesive story?

My concern is it sounds like a lot of this is backstory; and I generally don't vibe with that in a concept. My other concern is that you don't mention the Foundation at all in the pitch: the Foundation write the SCP article and hence are your POV characters, and so you need to like…have them actually take a protagonistic role in your story usually since everything has to be from their perspective.

item.title: Re: Adoption Poster: Scribbles!

I feel like this idea has a stronger plot progression than your other idea, and it in general feels stronger as a whole except for like…one detail: the why of it. Iunno what it is exactly, but I don't really vibe with the whole 'the bird is spying for Impending Bird Army Invasion' angle because it feels…weirdly grand as a followup for how grounded the rest is? It feels slightly like a jarringly large increase in stakes from 'a little spying' to 'oh yeah mass destruction', y'know? I think narrowing it in scope to like…maybe an Ocean's 11 style plot where they're trying to heist something and gathering information would work better, or like, the birds have been hired by some goi to gather info or something.

It might be worth tying Anderson Robotics in more here: like, at the moment they're mentioned in a weird offhand way that doesn't feel particularly relevant; but if the birds aims were tied in more, it could be a great way to have a bit of a twist ending or something. Alternatively, listen to nk and cut anderson completely.

This isn't really a 'how to kill the lizard' proposal, in the traditional sense, but I've always imagined that some bizarre but mundane object (e.g a finch with a tiny top hat)1 could kill it, but no ones tested that specific thing, so it just keeps on going.

item.title: An Exelent Dentist
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article,

Genre: Horror/Psychological/Humour

Elevator Pitch:
The story revolves around an Ontario police department detective who discovers a string of disappearances leading him to a supernatural encounter and eventually recruitment into the SCP.

The SCP appears as a normal Dentist, family man, well respected and successful.

Central Narrative:

The SCP in this article is both setting and a lead in to another story I have in mind. The central horror narrative will be within the debriefing log of the Detective character of the story. The SCP itself will be a combination of light and creepy.

The SCP is intended to be Benign with a twist in further tales but for this story will be the creation point of the Detectives Horror story.

+ show block
– hide block

The Detective is an single minded workaholic with a talent for pattern recognition. He has been very successful the last few years professionally but at a great cost to his personal life which is now nonexistent. His mental state is also fraying due to overwork and PTSD.

His story begins after a medically induced coma and short term amnestics is administered to temporarily block memories which are harmful to the detective.

The Detective is being debriefed by an SCP Psychologist. Over the course of the debrief the Detectives memories will be challenged and teased out as the Amnestics wear off allowing him to gradually confront the horror of the SCP's progeny erupting from a persons teeth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
First off. I have a reoccurring nightmare about my teeth crumbling and being forced to spit out the pieces. I have talked to many people who have a similar dream and the internet says it is a pretty common one. This scares the fuck out of me and I bet it does a lot of people. But that is the cheap scares part.

Ideally I want the debrief to play like a slow reveal of the psychological degradation of the detective as he confronts his emerging memories of the events. Leading up to the death of someone he knew and purposefully led to the dentist in an effort to catch the SCP abducting the victim.

Additional Notes:

It's been a few year since I put pen to paper and I am looking forward to seeing if this idea is any good. I got super excited so this is actually already in second draft on my side. Thank you in advance for any commentary.

The Snow is Deep

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
How does the computer communicate from the center of the earth? I honestly can't imagine just handwaving this sorta thing… how does a signal travel from an incorporeal electronic device to physical electronic devices, through miles and miles of solid mass?

It's a Foundation long-distance communicator utilizing anomalous tech. Given that the Foundation has communication methods that can communicate extra-dimensionally and that most types of communication are intangible anyway, I don't feel communicating with an intangible computer is much of a stretch. And Foundation technology pretty much renders distance and matter separations irrelevant.

Why are there so many bodies down there? Like what is happening to make this occur? I can't imagine people are being turned incorporeal this often… If they are, why isn't that the SCP and not the bodies at the center of the earth?

The anomaly is the collection of everyone who has ever become intangible and fallen through the floor and it has been building up over many thousands of years. The bodies come from as far-flung sources as ancient trickster gods, experimental para-technology from an Occult war and quite a few from previous iterations of SCP-2000. Lastly while most bodies are dead, none have decomposed due to their intangible nature. As for some central object or entity causing this, that's simply not the case. This isn't a sinister plot or experiment gone wrong, this is an inevitability in a world with intangibility.

+ show block
– hide block

If the agents are deaf, dumb and blind (I don't know why because the post doesn't say, but I assume because of their status deep in the earth)… how can they tell the Foundation anything? They have no sensation (because tactile is out, due to their incorporeality).

I still think there isn't much to this narrative. It feels like a description of people suffering… but what is the arc here? Just "we're intangible, and at the center of the earth!" and then dying? (Also how would the agents even know about that they're in the center of the earth?)

Good point. I have changed the original post to explain how the agents understand and can interact with their situation.

Which is that they don't.

To the agents, they have been plunged into complete darkness, unable to move or touch anything, with a faint sensation of things (the other intangible people) filling the same space as them. To the agent with the computer, the computer is an outlet through by which they can call for help and via which may one day be rescued. So they desperately type at the computer, relying solely on muscle memory, not knowing whether what they are typing is being revived and unable to know if anyone has replied. The narrative is the story of that agents' experience, how they go from fearing, to hopeful, to desperate, and the implication that many other people have gone through that experience without the chance of salvation and will continue doing so indefinitely. It's a description of people suffering, but the story of one of those people shows how hopeless, prolonged and empty that suffering is.

item.title: Re: The Black Hourglass
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there Dr Hajovsky. Let’s take a look at The Black Hourglass.

+ LBL
- LBL

Item #: SCP-#### The Black Hourglass

Formatting: remember to get rid of “The Black Hourglass” when you post it to the mainlist.

acting site director

Formatting: capitalise all titles.

After initial activation, researcher will be permitted to enter.

Grammar: missing “the” before “researcher”

Time spent within 10 meters of SCP-#### should be kept at an absolute minimum.

This statement is both confusing and vague. Should be reworked so you don’t get mixed up between duration and distance. Also, “absolute minimum” means… what? No longer than 10 minutes? 20 mins? It builds more tension if you included a specific maximum time before the researchers have to leave.

Dr. Licht and SCP-####'s locations are to be monitored at all times.

Isn’t the SCP already confined within the steel cage? Why would its location still need to be monitored then?

Dr. Licht is also not allowed to enter within 10 meters of any personnel

Grammar: you don’t “enter within 10 meters”. Rephrase to “be within” or “approach” or just give him a restraining order.

or civilian unless ordered to do so

This is an interesting condition. So he can approach other people, just that he has to be monitored in some way?

Overall, I’m a little confused by the conprocs, as you spend more time discussing Dr. Licht instead of the actual SCP. You’re setting up some kind of dual narrative here, and I’m intrigued but also worried if you’ll be able to pull off this complexity. Let’s see!

It is 18 cm long and 9 cm at its widest point.

A little glaring that you didn’t include the height.

Its outer layer is comprised of a black, metallic substance of unknown origin.

Similarly, a little glaring you didn’t tell us what its made of internally.

SCP-#### has the ability to create a temporal anomaly capable of consuming the time of macroscopic life within a radius of roughly 10 meters.

Okay, a lot to unpack here. It consumes “time” or “life”? I know you’re hinting at them to be one and the same, but it’s not clear enough. If it kills you, then just say as such, and how.

the length of time the anomaly consumes also appears random.

Grammar: “to be” before “appears”.

Upon activation, SCP-#### will emit several clicks, a loud, low droning sound, and other mechanical noises before quickly expanding and partially exposing the inside of the rectangular prism at its center.

This is detail better suited for your logs later on. I would cut it from the Description, which is meant to be more like an overall log of the scp’s properties.

SCP-#### appears to be designed to permanently bond itself to an humanoid individual, always remaining within a set distance no matter how much force is applied.

This effect came out of nowhere, and I’m not entirely sure why you included it. It’s also not particularly well explained – so the hourglass flies / hovers towards a bonded individual? Or just randomly appears? Need to clarify how this works.

SCP-#### was acquired by the foundation

“Foundation”.

after an anomalous event occurred in the sky above Site-19 on 08-0█-200█

First, there’s no need to tell us “an anomalous event occurred”. Just tell us directly what the anomalous event was. Second, and this is more of personal preference. I wouldn’t redact the year of events. Giving us the year allows the readers to sense where and when this story takes place.

Foundation staff present reported seeing a bright flash of blue light and hearing a loud explosion originating from a point approximately 100 meters above Site-19.

Should have started with this sentence.

While it remains unclear what the exact nature or cause of the anomaly was, it has been designated SCP-####-1.

Huh? Where did this designation come from? Are you referring to the sky event? I would personally cut this as you don’t want to overcomplicate the scp, especially when you’re focused on describing it.

After examining the crash site to make sure it was not biohazardous, Dr. Licht and SCP-#### were escorted by an on site containment team to a standard humanoid containment cell to await examination.

I would think the Foundation’s response would have been more agitated. If something crashed through the roof and suddenly attached itself to a personnel member, security would have quarantined him on the spot, weapons would be trained on the scp etc. This is too muted.

Nine minutes after crashing through the roof of Site-19, SCP-#### and Dr. Licht were being placed into a containment cell.

I don’t think this line is necessary. The information is repeated and redundant. Do we need to know that this specific thing happens after this specific amount of time?

on site containment team

“on-site”.

Contact was never reestablished with the containment team, however, remains with genetic matches to theirs were discovered at [DATA EXPUNGED].

Why is there a redaction here? Weren’t their remains discovered within the containment room?

Dr. Licht was later found in the cell, having suffered no adverse effects.

Okay, so he’s unharmed. But that’s it? What was his reaction? How was he behaving after such a traumatic event?

Addendum ####-02: Recorded Interview-1

The dialogue is generally okay, as is the pacing. What I’m not understanding is this theme of isolation and loneliness arising from Licht, mainly because it wasn’t ever mentioned before. Okay, so some guards died when the thing first arrived. You haven’t mentioned what else happens in between to show Licht’s isolation – does XXXX kill anyone who comes close? Can Licht see his family again? Need to emphasise this a little more before this log.

No tests have yet been conducted with other SCPs that exhibit anomalous corrosive or destructive properties.

Not sure why this line is relevant?

- Testing Documentation

Unsure if intentional, but you need to make this section more readable. Get rid of the mass italics, and use a table or block quotes instead.

Another issue: I don’t see the point of the test-logs. What exactly were you intending to show by this series of tests? To me, the effect seems entirely random: man lives, woman dies, arm disappears, guards disappear as well, man reappears somewhere else. What’s going on? Ideally, you should only include the most pertinent information that serve as variables in the tests. Here, you’re giving us too many details of the test subjects, which I’m assuming don’t actually matter to the results?

Dr. Licht: No, it's fine. I knew I was gonna have to talk about it eventually. [pauses] I was in there for what felt like days

Noting this is repeated info from the earlier audio log. I would cut either this or that.

Addendum ####-08: Containment Breach on 01-1█-0█

Ah? Licht used the object to breach containment? This doesn’t make sense. First, he’s a Foundation researcher. He knows the rules. Second, you haven’t given him a motivation prior to this to do so. Why does he do it? Does he want to visit his family? Has he grown to hate the Foundation because of what they’re doing to him?

Dr. Licht: Still, even if that's the case, I was never given the choice. This was still forced upon me by some cruel act of fate. And now, it feels like I don't have a choice in this either.

Do you see how he logic here doesn’t make sense? How does A=B? Unless the scp is forcing him to be random as well?

+ Overall
- Overall

(+/-) Concept. I’ll be honest: it’s all over the place. The early parts of the article made me think that the anomaly consumed “time” from individuals, thereby taking their lives. But the rest of the article quickly jumped all over the place to spatial displacement, immortality (now I know why you named him “Licht”, and a character arc that doesn’t always make sense.

I get that the focus here is on Licht’s story and how he deals with his newfound powers, but when writing a humanoid entity, you need to give him realistic goals first, and then follow him as he tries to attain them. Here, it seems the scp chose him entirely at random, and what follows are more random events that he gets himself into. If this was intentional btw (i.e., the cube is affecting him and making his actions random / harmful), the connection needs to be spelt out more.

I don’t know, really. You took the story in a different direction from how you set it up, and the payoff wasn’t very strong because the characters and their situations weren’t believable to me.

(+/-) Pacing. The article is too long. Large portions of the Description and Conprocs can be cut / refined to connect better with the rest of the story. I don’t understand what you were going for with the many test-logs – they too need to be refined in terms of direction. I do like the interview logs, though, and the growing relationship between Licht and Lachman. Each log doesn’t overstay its welcome, and the dialogue feels authentic, as are Licht’s emotions in the moment.

Overall, I’m leaning towards a downvote at this point. Reading your original greenlit post now, I would have cautioned you earlier to have linked your themes better. You mention you want a human-driven story of a person dealing with Fate. Okay, but how does that connect to time manipulation and other dimensions? Why does the scp sometimes kill people and at others, transport them through time and space? The link between these two effects needs to be explained better.

If you decide to revise the draft / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. For now, all the best with the writing!

item.title: SCP- Assimilator
item.content:encoded:
Item name: Assimilator

Greenlight: yes

Page layout: SCP article

Elevator pitch: A humanoid, resembling a male human, consisting of cells with anomalous biological characteristics, such as:

  • No presence of senescence.
  • Can modify their characteristics to provide enhanced regenerative abilities, and inhuman bursts of energy.
  • Immunity to all pathogens.

This SCP has been previously caught and studied, however it escaped Foundation custody and is now uncontained.

Central Narrative:
The cost of these properties is that the SCP needs more sustenance than a normal human. So, the entity finds it by eating food or hunting for live prey and/or carcasses to scavenge.

To hunt, it becomes a wraith-like mass consisting of mostly its cells to move like a swarm. Once in contact with prey, the mass encompasses it and begins stripping organic matter and nutrients from the organism, leaving only a husk. Once sated it returns to its normal form.

If the SCP gets severely injured, it will regenerate rapidly, however it will now need lots of energy replenishment, so it will consume large amounts of food or assimilate any living thing in its vicinity until sated.

The SCP can also shape shift into any creature by obtaining a sample of said creature’s DNA.

Hook/Attention:
The SCP creates backups for itself, in case it is destroyed, by infecting other creatures with its cells. The cells can also operate as a separate entity from the main body, which seeks out potential hosts.
Hosts fall into 3 categories:

"DORMANT": Cells lay low in the body, mimicking the host's cells to avoid an immune response and detection. Some become neurons to access the hosts memories and senses, and relays the information telepathically to the entity.

"ACTIVE": Upon the entity's order, cell replication rate increases and the cells take over the host, who is now under the control of the entity. The host is semi-sentient. This host will also mutate if severely damaged.

"REVIVAL": When sensing its destruction is imminent or when destroyed, the SCP’s cells in a particular host will begin replicating rapidly to replace the host with the entity. The reborn entity will retain all the memories of its previous body as well as the host's memories and skills.

The entity can also initiate rapid cellular degradation at will in itself to escape and revive in a host, or in an "ACTIVE" host to destroy it.

Hosts of SCP’s cells who are suffering from any disease or disorder, regardless of severity, will make a full recovery within 48 hours, assumed to be a by-product of the entity requiring a healthy host.

item.title: Want to earn Greenlighting Privileges and/or choose next month's front-page features?
item.content:encoded:
Due to the ever-increasing demand for more skilled reviewers to help out in the forums, the Forum Criticism Staff Team has been holding 2-week mentoring sessions to train up-and-coming reviewers. These are called "Flights".1

What does being part of a Flight mean?

  • Flight 1 will run from February 1 to February 15. Flight 2 will run from February 15 to February 30.
  • Mentors (dubbed "commanders") will work with mentees ("officers") in the Writing Help forums to critique concepts and drafts while the officers practice and improve their critique skills.
  • At the start of the Flight, officers will determine their weekly goals for two categories: activity and quality. Activity can be something simple like "crit at least one thread a day", quality something like "be more familiar with matching authors to helpful resources/guides/example articles". Commanders will discuss these goals weekly.
  • Officers will be taught some forum management skills like how to respond (without backseat modding) to a thread that breaks guidelines.
  • If the officers cannot yet greenlight, they may officially recommend concepts to their commander for greenlight consideration.
  • Flight teams can have funny/rule of cool names. Commander discretion.

Who are the commanders this month?

The commanders for Flight 1 are Karablue9482 and TBA.

The commanders for Flight 2 are TBA.

Notice: for February, we are opening up commander signups to all individuals who currently have greenlighting privileges! If you're interested in learning about being a commander/mentor, please look at this page for more information.

Who can request consideration to be an officer?

Anyone! Newbies and veterans alike are welcome to put their names forth.

What do Flight participants get at the end?

  • For as long as the mentorship system continues, Flight teams will select the featured SCP, tale, and GoI format displayed on the front page of the site. Flight team member names will also be displayed on the front page of the site.2
  • Officers deemed ready by their commanders will be given greenlighting privileges (if they do not have them already), and their names and number of successful Flights will be displayed on the Butterfly Squad Roster.
  • Flight team member names will be displayed on the corresponding month's Site News page. Officers may optionally provide "flight signoff" messages where they briefly describe the experience and any parting words for future reviewer mentees.
  • (remember, provision of the rewards is up to commander discretion!)
Footnotes
1. Prepare for some Rule of Cool terminology, folks.
2. To accommodate six teams, the number of monthly front page features will be doubled.

item.title: JANUARY 2021 INTROS - Readers & Reviewers
item.content:encoded:
Note: If you're going to introduce yourself here, please scroll down and click "New Post" and NOT "reply", otherwise your comment will nest incorrectly!

Hello, readers and reviewers of the Foundation Universe!

This month's random question is: what do you think is the best kind of food to eat with friends?

Let's start off with some things to take a look at to enhance your reading, now that you're a site member:

  • If you have any questions about the Foundation'verse and its various individuals and groups of interest, head over to the Foundation Universe forum to talk about the various aspects of living/working/being in constant fear of a world where anomalies are real.
  • Did you know our site has a night mode version? If you're interested in that (and a few other neat things!), check out our Usertools page.
  • Want to leave a comment or read others' thoughts on something you've read recently? Scroll down to the bottom of that page you read, click the "Discuss" link, and take a look at the comments others have posted!

For those looking to put your knowledge of the SCP-verse to work and contribute to the site by helping develop works-in-progress, head on over to the Writing Help forums!

  • So you want to be a concept reviewer?
  • So you want to be a draft reviewer?
  • And of course, remember the Criticism Policy!

If you're not sure what to talk about here, you can take a look at our How to Write an Intro/Welcome thread for ideas.

Go ahead and respond to other new members if you find that your interests overlap, and definitely ask for reading suggestions if there's a particular kind of SCP article or tale you enjoy reading. If you're looking to get started as a critiquer, feel free to mention the kind of material you particularly want to see more of on the wiki! You might even see some of our authors drop by here from time to time, if you mention you liked their work! :)

Welcome to the site!
